function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

message.reasoning: The user asks: "is any vpn is installed". They want to know if any VPN is installed. We need to check if any VPN software is installed on the system. We have a tool to run system commands. On Windows, we can query installed programs via registry or wmic. Let's use wmic product get name. That lists installed products. Then parse output for known VPN names like "OpenVPN", "Cisco AnyConnect", "NordVPN", etc. But we can't parse here; we just return the command execution result. So we call cmd_controller_execute with command "wmic product get Name" and maybe filter? We could use findstr to search for known VPN names. Let's do "wmic product get Name | findstr /i \"vpn\"". That will list any product containing "vpn". But some VPNs may not contain "vpn" in name. Better to list all and let user see. We'll just run "wmic product get Name" and return output.
